steps.say: Each anthracycline carries its own lifetime ceiling, and the exam tests the exact numbers rather than the concept alone. Epirubicin allows the highest total because its chemistry spares the heart, while idarubicin and mitoxantrone allow far smaller totals. Commit the five numbers as a ladder from nine hundred down to one forty. Crossing the ceiling converts a curative drug into a cardiac time bomb.
steps.tx: Every anthracycline (a family of red coloured cell killing drugs ending in rubicin) has a maximum lifetime cumulative dose (the total ever given), above which heart failure risk soars. **Epirubicin** (the 4 prime epimer of doxorubicin) allows 900 mg/m2 (milligrams per square metre of body surface), daunorubicin 550 to 600, doxorubicin 450 to 550, idarubicin 150 and mitoxantrone (an anthracenedione relative) 140. Epirubicin glucuronidation (liver sugar tagging) clears it faster with less intramyocardial free radical generation. These ceilings decide retreatment and trial eligibility.

steps.say: The biopsy finding has a memorable nickname that the exam loves to offer among lookalike options. Picture the heart cell ballooning with empty bubbles under the light microscope and losing its striped contractile threads under the electron beam. That paired picture is unique to anthracycline injury and is graded on the Billingham scale. No other drug produces this exact signature.
steps.tx: Anthracycline cardiotoxicity produces pathognomonic **Adria cells** (heart muscle cells damaged by Adriamycin, a trade name of doxorubicin), graded on endomyocardial biopsy (a catheter sample of heart tissue) by the Billingham scale. Light microscopy shows cytoplasmic vacuolar degeneration (bubble like swelling of the sarcoplasmic reticulum), while electron microscopy shows dropout and loss of myofibrils (the striped contractile threads) with Z band disruption. Iron chelation (iron binding) therapy and biopsy surveillance follow from this pathology in high dose protocols.

rows: Myofibrillar loss with Z band loss
Decides dose stop or iron chelation

steps.say: Timing questions separate anthracycline injury from other heart diseases, so anchor the one year window firmly. Risk climbs with every extra milligram and jumps steeply past six hundred. The exam pairs low dose percentages against high dose percentages to test whether you know the curve shape. Remember that the chronic progressive form dominates, not the acute infusion reaction.
steps.tx: Classic anthracycline cardiomyopathy (chronic progressive heart muscle failure) is cumulative and dose dependent, most commonly declaring itself **within 1 year** (the first twelve months) after completing therapy. Doxorubicin heart failure rates run about 3 to 5 percent at 400 mg/m2, 4 to 7 percent at 500 to 550 and above 36 percent at 600 or more. Antitumour action runs through DNA intercalation (drug wedging between base pairs) and topoisomerase II alpha blockade, while cardiac injury runs through the beta isoform discussed next.

steps.say: Two poisons work together inside the heart cell, and each one explains a different protective strategy. Iron driven free radicals shred mitochondrial membranes while topoisomerase beta blockade breaks cardiac DNA. Dexrazoxane counters both arms at once, which is why it remains the proven shield. The HER2 neighbourhood fact explains why some breast cancers melt faster under anthracyclines.
steps.tx: Cardiac injury flows from myocardial oxidative damage by iron catalysed **reactive oxygen species** (ROS, unstable molecules from quinone redox cycling) plus cardiomyocyte topoisomerase II beta (Top2B, a DNA untangling enzyme) poisoning. Dexrazoxane (an iron chelator that also degrades Top2B) prevents both arms. The TOP2A gene (encoding the tumour target Top2 alpha) sits beside ERBB2 (HER2) on chromosome 17q12 to 21 and is co amplified in 35 to 40 percent of HER2 positive breast cancers, heightening anthracycline sensitivity there.

points: Iron ROS plus Top2 beta poisoning
right.title: Heart Injury Top2 Beta

steps.say: Prevention questions usually hide one false protector among three real ones, so test each option against the proven list. Dexrazoxane leads once the doxorubicin total passes three hundred, with liposomal packaging and slow infusion as the other shields. Ivabradine slows the sinus node but never prevented cardiomyopathy. Apply the ESC numbers for dysfunction exactly as written.
steps.tx: Proven cardioprotection means **dexrazoxane** (the Top2B degrading iron chelator) once doxorubicin exceeds 300 mg/m2 at a 10 to 1 dose ratio, liposomal doxorubicin (fat bubble packs) or continuous infusion over 6 to 96 hours lowering peaks. Ivabradine (a sinus node If channel blocker) does not prevent cardiomyopathy and is the classic EXCEPT answer. ESC defines cancer therapy related cardiac dysfunction as a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF, pumping percentage) drop above 10 points to below 50 percent or a relative global longitudinal strain (GLS, fibre shortening) fall above 15 percent.
